title: Where the ping gets lost
instruction: Estimate the result. Light travels at 300,000 km/s in a vacuum and about 200,000 km/s in glass fibre. Ping is the time there and back.

items.q: How many kilometres does a signal travel in fibre in 1 millisecond?
items.why: 200,000 km a second is 200 km per thousandth of a second. So every 100 km of cable adds 1 ms to the ping: half a millisecond there and half back.

items.q: The smallest possible ping from Prague to New York (about 6,600 km), if the fibre ran straight.
items.why: There and back is 13,200 km, and 13,200 ÷ 200,000 = 0.066 s. The real ping is usually around 100 ms, because the cable doesn’t run straight and routers hold the packet for a moment.

items.q: Internet through a geostationary satellite at a height of 36,000 km. How much ping does the journey alone add? The signal goes up and down on the way there, then up and down on the way back.
items.why: 4 × 36,000 = 144,000 km at 300,000 km/s is 0.48 s. For a fast shooter that’s hopeless, even if the satellite were perfect in every other way.

items.q: A satellite in low orbit at a height of 550 km. How many milliseconds does the journey up and down, there and back, add?
items.why: 4 × 550 = 2,200 km, divided by 300,000 km/s is about 0.007 s. That’s why networks of low satellites have a ping similar to cable. But there have to be thousands of them in orbit, because each one is above you for only a few minutes.

items.q: A game runs at 60 frames per second. How many milliseconds does one frame have?
items.why: 1,000 ms ÷ 60 ≈ 16.7 ms. In that time the game has to calculate the physics and draw the whole picture.

items.q: You have a ping of 100 ms and the game runs at 60 frames per second. How many frames later does the server find out about your shot?
items.why: Only half the ping leads to the server, so 50 ms. 50 ÷ 16.7 = 3 frames. That’s why games predict movement, and the server works out afterwards where the opponent was standing at the moment of the shot.

items.q: A 4K stream needs 25 Mb/s (megabits per second). How many MB (megabytes) do you download in a minute? 1 byte = 8 bits.
items.why: 25 ÷ 8 = 3.125 MB/s, times 60 is 187.5 MB. Speed in Mb/s and delay in ms are two different things: a wider motorway doesn’t make the trip to Australia shorter.

debrief: Delay has a hard lower limit: the speed of light times the length of the cable. On top of that, routers, queues and the server add time. A faster connection gives you more data per second, but it doesn’t shorten the ping. Only a server closer to you does that.
